answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a spiral as the anchor of the cost.
